$comment: What a fixture must carry to count as evidence. §16.2 lists nine things the evaluation set must include, and a fixture missing any of them is a file someone will later have to guess about. The §7.1 categories are NOT listed here: they are read out of the case study, because a list copied into this file would be checked against the copy.

source.$comment: Where the categories to cover come from. A floor, not a count: adding a disclosure category must not fail, and removing one must not pass.

provenance.$comment: §16.2's nine requirements, as fields every fixture must carry. Counted from the source rather than from memory - §9.1 was miscounted once here, and the wrong number reached an acceptance criterion before anyone noticed.
provenance.driftTest: tools/test-fixtures.mjs regenerates every fixture and compares the hash, so a file edited by hand fails rather than quietly becoming its own label

kinds.$comment: Every §7.1 category needs both. A detector that fires on the positive and also on the control has found nothing; §17.1 puts clean controls wrongly given a blocking deterministic finding at 0.
kinds.must_detect: carries the disclosure the category names, and a detector that misses it is a release blocker (§17.1)
kinds.clean_control: resembles the positive as closely as possible without carrying the disclosure, and must produce no blocking deterministic finding

generation.$comment: Written as raw PDF syntax by a script, not produced by a library. A library's output carries that library's habits - object numbering, compression, metadata it adds unasked - and a fixture is supposed to isolate one thing. Raw syntax is also reviewable in a diff, which a binary is not.
generation.deterministic: byte-identical across runs and machines; no timestamps, no random object ids, no compression
generation.noRealData: §16.1 forbids committing real personal information. Every value here is invented and obviously so.

category_uncovered.rationale: a §7.1 category has no fixture. The detection rate this repository reports is a fraction, and a category with no fixture is missing from the denominator - which reads as full coverage of a smaller requirement.

provenance_incomplete.rationale: a fixture is missing one of §16.2's nine fields. The missing one is always the one someone needs later, and by then the person who knew has gone.

fixture_drifted.rationale: a fixture's bytes do not match what its generator produces. A fixture edited by hand becomes its own label, and the label it was given stops describing it.

refusals.$comment: Each refusal says where its negative case lives. in_suite means the suite breaks it on a copy and watches the reason come back; in_ci means reaching it requires editing the source of truth, which only a mutation case can do - and the suite then checks the workflow carries one, because a reason whose negative lives nowhere is a claim about enforcement that does not happen.
